clinician.trajectory_summary: An 83-year-old man with a history of cardiac disease presented with acute febrile illness, mental confusion, drowsiness, and signs of systemic inflammation including hypotension and tachycardia. Initial laboratory findings showed renal dysfunction, mild liver involvement, elevated LDH and CRP, normochromic macrocytic anemia, and severe thrombocytopenia. Systemic infection workup, including blood cultures, procalcitonin, and viral antibodies, was negative, although a positive urine culture for E. coli was noted. Further investigation revealed hyperferritinemia (2656 ng/ml), hypertriglyceridemia (343 mg/dl), splenomegaly (15.5 cm), and coexistent aspects of hemophagocytosis in the bone marrow, fulfilling multiple diagnostic criteria for HLH.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with fever, mental confusion, drowsiness, hypotension, and tachycardia.

Initial labs showed elevated BUN (159 mg/dl), creatinine (1.99 mg/dl), hyperkalemia (5.9 mEq/L), elevated LDH (2494 IU/L), CRP (5.96 mg/dl), normochromic macrocytic anemia (Hb = 11.2 g/dl), severe thrombocytopenia (30,000/µL), and mild hypertransaminasemia (AST = 141 UI/l, ALT= 40 UI/L).
Blood cultures, procalcitonin, and viral antibodies were negative, ruling out common systemic infections.
Splenomegaly (bipolar diameter = 15.5 cm) was identified on ultrasound.
Bone marrow examination revealed coexistent aspects of hemophagocytosis.
